intro: Money is everywhere. You see it at the store. You see prices on signs. Grown-ups earn money at work. In this unit you will learn what money is for.
You will learn coins and what they are worth. You will pay and count change. You will make a plan to save, spend and share your money.
At the end, you can make a plan for your own money. You can wait for something big. You can help others too. You will know how money works.
bigQuestion: What is money for, and how can I use it well?

timeline.t: People trade things, like a cookie for an apple
Trading gets stuck when people want different things
People agree to use money to trade
We learn coins: penny, nickel, dime, quarter
We read prices and pay, then count our change
We earn money by doing work
We save, spend and share with three jars
We keep money safe in a bank

words.d: to give something and get something back, when both people agree
trading things for other things, without money
coins and bills that people agree to take when they buy and sell
money you get back when you pay more than the price
to get money for doing work
to keep money now so you can use it later
a business that keeps people's money safe

choices: Giving something and getting something back
test.why: In a trade, both people swap.

test.q: Why is money easier than barter?
test.why: People agree to take money, so trading is easy.

test.q: How many cents is a nickel?
Which coin is worth the most?
test.why: A quarter is 25 cents, the most here.

test.q: A toy costs 60 cents (an example). You pay $1. What is your change?
How do most people get money?
test.why: Most people earn money at work.

test.q: A ball costs $3 (an example). You save $1 a week. How many weeks?
What are the three jars for?
test.why: The three jars split money three ways.
A bank keeps your money safe.

test.q: You have $1. You buy a sticker for $1. What do you give up?
test.why: One dollar can be spent or saved, not both.

write.prompt: You earn $3 a week (an example). You want a $6 kite (an example). Make a plan. How much will you save, spend and share each week? How many weeks until the kite?
tips: Say how much goes in each jar.
Say what you give up to wait.
Tell why your plan is a good one.
